intro.title: Flex shorthand and patterns
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, responsive webpage layout using CSS Flexbox. You will learn the core concept of the flex shorthand property, which combines flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis into a single declaration. The main technologies involved are CSS and the Flexbox layout model. By applying common flex patterns, you'll create flexible containers and items that adjust to different screen sizes. This will help you write cleaner, more efficient CSS for modern web designs.
intro.usecase: Flex shorthand is essential for building responsive, component-based layouts in modern web applications. Developers use it daily to quickly arrange navigation bars, card grids, and dashboard panels that adapt to different screen sizes. For example, a product listing page on an e-commerce site uses flex shorthand to align product cards in a grid, ensuring consistent spacing and alignment. Similarly, a settings panel in a web app relies on flex patterns to stack form labels and inputs neatly, improving readability and user interaction.
